errors.english: When other monks asked, "What will happen if you do that?" he replied, "The alms bowl might break." Because it was not proper, the bowl eventually fell and broke.
errors.why: The monks told him "Don't do that"; he asked "What will happen?"; they answered "The bowl will break"; he did not comply (མ་བཏུབ་པས) and the bowl fell and broke — speakers are swapped and the refusal is misread as "not proper".

fix.find: When other monks asked, "What will happen if you do that?" he replied, "The alms bowl might break." Because it was not proper, the bowl eventually fell and broke.
fix.replace: When the monks told him, "Do not do that," he asked, "What will happen?" They said, "The alms bowl will break," but he did not comply, and the bowl fell and broke.

note: A faithful rendering of the śaikṣa rules on bowls and teaching posture, except that the dialogue in the standing-washing story is inverted.

errors.english: the habituation of engaging in meaningless entities and so forth
errors.why: དོན་མེད་པ here means objectless/without a real referent: habituation to engaging in [notions of] entity etc. that have no object, not "meaningless entities".

errors.english: because that external entity has already been clarified
errors.why: The context (internal entity likewise already refuted, བཀག་ཏུ་ཟིན) requires བསལ་ཟིན་པ, 'has already been refuted/excluded', not 'clarified'.

note: The rebirth argument (homogeneous seed, svabhāvahetu, exclusion of the external object) is followed correctly; two terms are off.

errors.english: (Nagarjuna) the foundational master of the Middle Way school, circa 2nd century CE
errors.why: The verse only says 'Nāgārjuna holds thus'; the identification and date are unmarked translator material inserted into the verse.

note: Verses from Nāgārjuna, Āryadeva and the sūtras and the Cārvāka verse are rendered accurately; only unmarked inline glosses intrude.

errors.english: in order to find fault with the claim that positive and negative pervasions are not established, the opponent argues
errors.why: The opponent raises the objection THAT anvaya and vyatireka are not established; he is not attacking that claim.

fix.find: in order to find fault with the claim that positive and negative pervasions are not established, the opponent argues
fix.replace: in order to raise the objection that the positive and negative pervasions are not established, the opponent argues

errors.why: The Sanskrit for དངོས་པོ is bhāva; 'bhavat' is not the term.

errors.english: those things that do not depend on anything else are certain to exist, just as, for example, the final collection of causes [note: The set of conditions immediately preceding an effect] is what produces a result.
errors.why: The proof form says: what is independent with respect to X is certain to have X, like the final causal complex with respect to producing its effect; the English turns it into 'certain to exist' and loses the 'independent with respect to producing the effect' of the example.

note: The momentariness debate is broadly followed, but the opponent's objection is inverted and the formal statement of the proof is garbled.

errors.english: obscured by the cataracts of ignorance regarding the clinging to a self
errors.why: The Daśabhūmika lists two attributes: (the childish) cling to a self, and are obscured by the cataract of ignorance; it is not 'ignorance regarding clinging to a self'.

note: The Daśabhūmika quotation and the argument that self-view is the ignorance-limb are rendered soundly.

errors.english: appears to be connected to the term "no annihilation" by way of an interval.
errors.why: The alternative explanation concludes 'therefore the word "non-cessation" is placed first', which is dropped (and ཡང་ན 'alternatively' is rendered 'furthermore').

note: The Prajñāpāramitā dialogue and the commentary on the order of the negations are accurate apart from one dropped conclusion.
Accurate treatment of ātyayika robes, the cīvara season with and without kaṭhina, the exceptions, and the start of the forest-dweller rule.

errors.english: Ka. [note: This letter marks the beginning of the section or volume.]
errors.why: ཀ་ནི is the tail of a Sanskrit word continued from the previous side (…karṇikāni), not a section marker.

fix.find: Ka. [note: This letter marks the beginning of the section or volume.]

errors.english: He stood tall like the (Parijata) the wish-fulfilling tree of the gods among the (Sura) demigods or celestial beings
errors.why: The Sanskrit surakṣitiruhām shows the comparison is the pārijāta among the trees of the gods, not among gods/demigods.

errors.english: the (Sugata) Well-Gone One; the Buddha was seen nearby, seated upon them
errors.why: What is seen placed on the lotuses is the Sugata's wheel (sugatacakram, the wheel-marked feet); the 'wheel' is dropped and the image becomes the Buddha seated.

note: The Tibetan verses of this bilingual side are rendered in outline, but with a false section-marker note and several imagery errors.

errors.english: those who are as stable as the Mountains of King in the salt water ocean
errors.why: The compound means firm like those two, the ocean and the king of mountains, not a mountain standing in the ocean.

fix.find: those who are as stable as the Mountains of King in the salt water ocean
fix.replace: those who are as firm as the ocean and the king of mountains

errors.english: The phrases (Sage) Muni, (Chief of the Herd), (Ascetic) Shramana, and (Lord of Beings) are all words of address.
errors.why: There are three vocatives (Sage, Bull, Lord of the śramaṇa folk), and only the last is glossed as 'chief of ārya persons', whereas the English splits it into four and applies the gloss to all.
With the previous side: pride is being puffed up with regard to one's own qualities; ལྟོས་པ is 'with regard to', not 'comparison'.

errors.english: (by showing the spoken words) and (by the supreme virtues)
errors.why: The commentary immediately glosses brtan pa, dam pa and dge ba as qualities of the words: 'by words that are firm, excellent and virtuous'.

note: A word-commentary on a hymn whose lemma-gloss structure is often misparsed, though the individual glosses are mostly right.

errors.why: This glosses the root-verse words: 'entity' means arising (coming to be from not having been), and 'is not' (མེད་པ) means 'is impossible', so the entity is impossible; the English instead asserts that non-existence is impossible.

fix.replace: and "does not exist" means that it is impossible

note: The arising/destruction argument and the produced/unproduced dilemma are rendered well apart from one misread gloss.
